subject: Order Form: Dalton Health - staggered commit schedule and tax/invoice flow
messages:
From: Sam Torres <s.torres@daltonhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: payments@daltonhealth.com
Date: 2028-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form: Dalton Health - staggered commit & tax flow

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Dalton wants to move forward but needs the order form to reflect a staggered commit schedule to match our funding tranches. High level: 3 tranches across 12 months (40% / 30% / 30%), invoiced on execution, month 6 and month 12 respectively. A few asks from our side before we sign:

- We need clarity on invoice timing and net terms for each tranche. Can the first invoice be Net 60 and subsequent ones Net 30? Our procurement team prefers that structure.
- Dalton may withhold up to 5% for tax purposes depending on jurisdiction—will Redwood gross up or provide an alternative?
- PO requirement: we must issue a PO number before the first invoice; please confirm whether Redwood can accept a PO and whether the PO number can be added post-execution if required.
- Any holdback or commissioning credit mechanics (e.g., delay credits) need to be explicit. For internal cashflow reasons we'd like a short holdback (5%) released after the first 60 days of activation.
- Please share any evidence we need to provide (tax residency, W-8/W-9) to avoid withholding. I attached our tax residency certificate for your records.

Can you circulate a short set of redlineable clauses that addresses the above? We want to minimize legal back-and-forth.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Procurement, Dalton Health
payments@daltonhealth.com

Attachment: Dalton_Tax_Certificate.pdf (pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: payments@daltonhealth.com, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Dalton Health - staggered commit & tax flow

Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the certificate. We can work with the staggered tranches. Initial thoughts:

- Invoicing schedule: first tranche invoiced on execution (Net 60), tranche 2 and 3 invoiced on 6-month and 12-month anniversaries of execution (we can do Net 30 on those).
- PO acceptance: Redwood can accept a PO before the first invoice; adding the PO number post-execution is acceptable but we need a written confirmation from Dalton procurement within 7 days of execution to avoid processing delays.
- Holdback / commissioning credit: propose a 3% commissioning holdback (applied to total invoice amount) released 60 days after activation; if activation is delayed >30 days from execution, a commissioning credit equal to the pro-rated holdback will apply to the next invoice.
- Withholding tax: Redwood prefers clients to provide tax residency docs (W-8/W-9 or local cert). We can include a 'gross-up' option if Dalton requests Redwood to bear any withholding, but we typically require supporting government receipts within 60 days of withholding. Alternatively, Dalton can remit a grossed-up amount on the invoice.

I've drafted a short tranche schedule and clause snippets and attached Draft_OrderForm_TrancheSchedule_v1.pdf for your legal/procurement review. If Dalton is okay with the proposed 3% holdback and the Net 60 / Net 30 split, I'll loop in our legal and finance teams to produce redlines.

Best,

1) Invoicing & Net terms: client wants Net 60 on T1, Net 30 thereafter. Finance would prefer uniform terms if possible.
2) Holdback: I proposed 3% (instead of their 5%) to limit impact on Redwood cashflow and keep Dalton happy; need explicit release/trigger language (60 days after activation).
3) Withholding / gross-up: need a clear approach: do we accept gross-up obligation, require receipts, or prefer client to gross up? Also need fallback if Dalton does not provide receipts within 60 days.
4) PO timing: confirm we can accept PO after execution but need written procurement confirmation within 7 days.
5) Usage true-up: recommend a quarterly true-up clause if their usage dips below the committed tranche (they raised this on call).

Irene — quick redlines / recommendations from Legal:

- Net terms: propose Net 45 uniformly across all three tranche invoices. A single term reduces administration and risk. If Dalton insists on Net 60 for the first invoice, accept it but convert all subsequent invoices to Net 45 instead of Net 30. (Reason: collections cadence and intercompany cash ops.)

- Holdback: reduce to 3% (ok) but prefer release tied to a defined "activation" milestone rather than a calendar day. Suggested language: "3% holdback of the invoice amount shall be released 60 days after Redwood confirms production activation as defined in Schedule A."

- Withholding/Gross-up: we should avoid an open gross-up obligation. Recommend this approach: If Dalton withholds taxes, Dalton shall provide official government withholding receipts within 60 days; Redwood will credit amounts properly documented. If receipts are not provided within 60 days, Redwood may invoice the withheld amount as a separate invoice and will pursue bilateral resolution — Redwood will not unilaterally gross-up unless explicitly agreed in writing by Finance/Legal leadership.

- PO: allowable post-execution inclusion is fine but require the procurement confirmation email to be attached to the invoice for AP processing.

- Usage true-up: add a quarterly true-up clause. If actual usage for a tranche period is below 90% of committed units, the parties will reconcile with a credit or invoice adjustment within 45 days of quarter end.

I've attached a short redline (in-text snippets) — happy to draft a redlined order form if you want.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Sam — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Summary of proposed compromise (please confirm in writing):

- Tranche schedule: 40% at execution (Invoice 1), 30% at month 6 (Invoice 2), 30% at month 12 (Invoice 3).
- Net terms: Invoice 1 — Net 45 (Redwood requested compromise); Invoice 2 & 3 — Net 30. If Dalton must have Net 60 for Invoice 1, please flag and we will accept conditionally but will require written procurement confirmation on PO and a signed amendment to the payment schedule.
- Holdback: 3% holdback of each tranche invoice; released 60 days after Redwood confirms production activation (activation definition in Schedule A). If activation is delayed >30 days from execution, a commissioning credit equal to the pro-rated holdback will be applied to the next invoice.
- Withholding tax: Dalton should provide official government withholding receipts or tax-residency docs within 60 days of any withheld amount. Redwood will credit properly documented withholdings. If receipts are not provided within 60 days, Redwood reserves the right to invoice the withheld amount separately pending bilateral reconciliation; Redwood will not gross-up unilaterally without written agreement.
- PO: PO number acceptable post-execution but must be confirmed in procurement email within 7 days; please attach PO confirmation to the invoice.
- Usage true-up: quarterly true-up with reconciliation within 45 days of quarter end if actual usage < 90% of committed units.

I've attached the current draft clause set for quick review. If Dalton confirms the above, I'll circulate a redlined order form (we can do DocuSign after internal sign-off).

Looking forward to your confirmation so we can move to signature.

Best,
Irene Choi
